sources.author: David Becker
sources.title: Moondrop Aria Review - Aim High
sources.excerpt: Aria has good midrange clarity, resolution and detail retrieval.

claims.quote: The bass seems a tad tighter and has a faster decay than the Starfield but still has plenty of drive and gusto.
While the midrange isn't what I would call full-bodied, it doesn't sound thin either but rather finds the middle ground.
Detail retrieval is good and while it's not the most precise or sparkly treble, it adds ample clarity and definition.
Aria has good midrange clarity, resolution and detail retrieval.
It has excellent build quality and comfort plus it just sounds darn good.

sources.author: Kazi
sources.title: Moondrop Aria (2021) Review (2) - The Big "Little" Upgrade

claims.quote: The bass reaches all the way down to 20Hz and provides excellent rumble.
The male vocals sound somewhat distant, although they're perfectly intelligible.
The treble rolls off fast post 11KHz and doesn't really offer a lot of sparkle or air.
Staging is good overall in terms of width/height, though stage depth is lacking vs the higher-tier IEMs.
Due to its snug-fit and lightweight nature, the Aria has very good wearing comfort.
Stock cable forms kinks, gets tangled in pocket

The treble has a good amount of sparkle and airiness without ever being sibilant or harsh.

sources.author: Jasper Lastoria
sources.title: Moondrop Aria review
sources.excerpt: Isolation won't blow anybody away, so if that's a high priority you might look elsewhere, or upgrade ear tips to memory foam.

claims.quote: This is a pretty dead on bass response.
Isolation won't blow anybody away, so if that's a high priority you might look elsewhere, or upgrade ear tips to memory foam.
It's comfortable for about 90 minutes, but the over-ear cabling feels a little annoying from go.
